content.focus: Algebra 1 teaches students to read, write and solve the language of mathematics. Students work with expressions, exponents, radicals and polynomials, solve equations and inequalities, build and graph linear functions and systems, factor and solve quadratics, model growth and decay with exponentials, and analyze data. The course aligns to the Florida B.E.S.T. Mathematics standards for Algebra 1 and ends with a cumulative problem set and a 15 question final exam. Excellence, Faith, Purpose.
content.title: Algebra 1
content.subject: Mathematics

title: Assessment 1: Expressions and Polynomials, Show Your Work

content.prompt: Show every step. (1) Evaluate 4x² − 5x + 2 when x = 3. (2) Simplify (2a³b)³. (3) Simplify √98 + √32. (4) Subtract (7x² + 3x − 4) − (2x² − x + 6). (5) Multiply (3x − 2)(x + 5). (6) In your own words, explain what each part of C = 12h + 35 means for a mechanic who charges by the hour.
content.rubric: Total 100. Items 1 to 5 are worth 15 each, with 10 for the correct answer and 5 for clear work. Item 6 is worth 25: identifies the coefficient 12 as the hourly rate, identifies the constant 35 as a one time fee, and uses full sentences.

title: Assessment 2: Equations and Inequalities, Show Your Work

content.prompt: Show every step. (1) Solve 7x − 3 = 4x + 15 and check. (2) Solve 2(3x − 1) = 5x + 7. (3) Solve A = ½h(b₁ + b₂) for h. (4) Solve and graph −4x + 3 > 11. (5) Solve |3x − 6| = 12. (6) Write and solve an equation or inequality for this situation: a church van rental costs $90 plus $0.50 per mile, and the youth ministry can spend at most $200. How many miles can they drive?
content.rubric: Total 100. Items 1 to 5 are worth 15 each (10 for the answer, 5 for work shown). Item 6 is worth 25: correct inequality 0.5m + 90 ≤ 200 (10), solves to m ≤ 220 (10), answers in a sentence with units (5).

title: Assessment 3: Functions and Linear Models, Show Your Work

content.prompt: Show every step. (1) Is {(1, 4), (2, 4), (3, 7)} a function? Explain. (2) If f(x) = 2x² − x, find f(−2). (3) Find the slope through (−1, 4) and (3, −4). (4) Write the equation of the line through (2, 7) with slope 3. (5) Write the equation of the line through (0, 5) perpendicular to y = ½x − 1. (6) A youth group washes cars. They start with $50 and earn $8 per car. Write a model, find the money after 12 cars, state a sensible domain, and tell how many cars give $250.
content.rubric: Total 100. Items 1 to 5 are worth 14 each (answer 10, work 4). Item 6 is worth 30: model y = 8x + 50 (8), 12 cars gives $146 (6), domain whole numbers x ≥ 0 (6), 25 cars (6), clear sentences (4).

title: Assessment 4: Systems and Inequalities, Show Your Work

content.prompt: Show every step. (1) Solve by graphing: y = −x + 6 and y = 2x. (2) Solve by substitution: y = 4x − 3 and 2x + y = 9. (3) Solve by elimination: 3x + 2y = 16 and x − 2y = 0. (4) Graph y ≥ x − 2 and describe the line and shading. (5) A youth fundraiser sells small cups at $2 and large cups at $3. They sell 60 cups and collect $150. Write a system and find how many of each. (6) A church van holds at most 15 people. Adults (a) and children (c) both ride. Write the constraints, graph the feasible region, and list two viable groups.
content.rubric: Total 100. Items 1 to 4 are worth 14 each. Item 5 is worth 20: system s + l = 60 and 2s + 3l = 150 (8), solution 30 small and 30 large (8), checked (4). Item 6 is worth 24: constraints a + c ≤ 15, a ≥ 0, c ≥ 0 (10), graph (8), two viable groups (6).

title: Assessment 5: Polynomials, Factoring and Quadratics, Show Your Work

content.prompt: Show every step. (1) Factor completely: x² + 8x + 15, 9x² − 49, and 2x² − 7x + 3. (2) Solve x² − 3x − 10 = 0 by factoring. (3) Solve 2x² + 5x − 3 = 0 with the quadratic formula. (4) For y = x² + 2x − 8, give the axis of symmetry, the vertex, the y intercept and the zeros, and tell whether the vertex is a maximum or a minimum. (5) Write a quadratic with zeros 2 and 5 that passes through (0, 20). (6) A rocket model has height h(t) = −16t² + 96t + 4 feet. Find the time of the peak, the maximum height, and explain in a sentence why the negative time answer is rejected when finding the landing time.
content.rubric: Total 100. Item 1: 18 (6 each). Item 2: 12 (x = 5 or x = −2). Item 3: 14 (discriminant 49, x = 1/2 or x = −3). Item 4: 20 (axis x = −1, vertex (−1, −9), y intercept (0, −8), zeros 2 and −4, minimum). Item 5: 12 (a = 2, y = 2(x − 2)(x − 5)). Item 6: 24 (peak at 3 seconds 8, maximum height 148 feet 8, reason that time cannot be negative 8). Show of work counts in every item.

title: Assessment 6: Exponential Functions, Models and Data, Show Your Work

content.prompt: Show every step. (1) A savings account holds $2,000 and earns 4% interest compounded yearly. Write the model, find the balance after 3 years, and compare it with simple interest for 3 years. (2) A computer worth $1,200 loses 25% of its value each year. Write the model and find the value after 2 years. (3) Describe the transformation from f(x) = x² to g(x) = −(x − 3)² + 2, and state the vertex. (4) For the data 2, 4, 4, 6, 8, 10, 30, find the mean, the median, Q1, Q3 and IQR, decide whether 30 is an outlier, and say which measure of center you would report. (5) A line of best fit is y = 3x + 10 for x, hours of practice per week, and y, number of free throws made out of 50. Predict y for x = 5, interpret the slope, and explain why x = 30 is unreliable.
content.rubric: Total 100. Item 1: 22 (A = 2000(1.04)ᵗ 6, balance $2,249.73 8, simple interest $240 giving $2,240 compared 8). Item 2: 16 (V = 1200(0.75)ᵗ 8, $675 8). Item 3: 16 (reflected over the x axis 4, right 3 4, up 2 4, vertex (3, 2) 4). Item 4: 26 (mean 64/7 about 9.14 4, median 6 4, Q1 4 4, Q3 10 4, IQR 6 4, outlier test 19 so 30 is an outlier 4, median recommended 2). Item 5: 20 (25 6, slope meaning 6, extrapolation 8). Show of work counts in every item.

content.prompt: Show every step for each item. (1) Simplify (2x³)(3x²) and write 5² · 5³ as a power of 5. (2) Simplify √48. (3) Multiply (x + 3)(x − 2). (4) Solve 3x − 7 = 11 and solve 2x + 5 < 11, and graph the inequality's solution on a number line in words. (5) Solve |x − 2| = 5. (6) Find the slope of the line through (1, 2) and (3, 8) and write its equation. (7) Solve the system y = 2x + 1 and x + y = 7 and check the solution. (8) Factor x² + 3x − 10 and solve x² − 5x + 6 = 0. (9) For y = x² − 4x + 3, give the axis, vertex and zeros. (10) A balance of $1,000 earns 5% interest compounded yearly. Write the model and find the balance after 2 years. (11) For the data 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, find the mean, median and IQR. (12) In two or three sentences, explain how you used one concept from this course in a real situation, and give glory to God for the gift of learning.
content.rubric: Total 100. Items 1 to 11 are worth 8 each (answer 5, work 3) for 88. Item 12 is worth 12 (relevant concept 4, clear explanation 4, reflection 4). Expected answers: 1) 6x⁵, 5⁵; 2) 4√3; 3) x² + x − 6; 4) x = 6 and x < 3; 5) x = 7 or x = −3; 6) slope 3, y = 3x − 1; 7) (2, 5); 8) (x + 5)(x − 2), and x = 2 or x = 3; 9) axis x = 2, vertex (2, −1), zeros 1 and 3; 10) A = 1000(1.05)ᵗ, $1,102.50; 11) mean 9, median 9, IQR 6. A score of 70 or better is required to pass.

content.prompt: Name one place in daily life, in ministry, or in a trade where an expression or formula is used. Describe the quantities involved and what each part of the formula means. Respond in 100 to 150 words.

Jesus said that a builder first sits down and counts the cost. Describe a real decision where you used or could use an equation or an inequality to set a budget or a limit. What were the variables? Respond in 100 to 150 words.

title: Discussion 3: A Rate in My Life

content.prompt: Describe one rate of change in your life or ministry, such as miles per hour, dollars per week, or members per month. Identify the starting value and the rate, and write a linear model. Respond in 100 to 150 words.
Describe a real situation where two conditions had to be true at the same time, such as a budget and a schedule. How could a system of equations or inequalities help? Respond in 100 to 150 words.

title: Discussion 5: The Shape of a Rise

content.prompt: A parabola goes down before it comes up, or up before it comes down. Describe a time in your life or ministry that felt like a vertex, a turning point. What changed after it? Explain how the idea of a maximum or a minimum helps you think about it. Respond in 100 to 150 words.

title: Discussion 6: Numbers That Tell the Truth

content.prompt: Describe a statistic or a growth pattern you have seen used in a news story, a social media post or a ministry report. Was it presented honestly? Explain what extra information, such as an outlier, the median, or the difference between correlation and causation, would help you judge it. Respond in 100 to 150 words.
